title: Democratic backsliding is broadening across regime types as expression, elections, civil society, and opposition protections deteriorate together
source_unit: V-Dem Institute, Democracy Report 2026: Unraveling the Democratic Era?, 10th edition, using V-Dem Dataset v16
geography: Global country-year democracy assessment, with regional analysis of Europe, North America, and autocratizing countries

observations.period: 2025; global regime distribution and population exposure

denominator.unit: countries assessed in the V-Dem global democracy framework, summarized as 92 autocracies and 87 democracies at end-2025

autocracies.unit: countries classified as autocracies at the end of 2025

democracies.unit: countries classified as democracies at the end of 2025

autocratic_population.unit: percent of the world population living in autocracies, approximately 6 billion people

liberal_democratic_population.unit: percent of the world population living in liberal democracies, approximately 0.6 billion people

democratic_level.value: the report assesses democracy for the average global citizen as returning to approximately 1978 levels

observations.method: V-Dem multidimensional democracy measurement using Dataset v16, country-year indicators, high-level indices, and regime-transformation analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Regime classifications and indices depend on coding, expert judgments, aggregation choices, and model definitions; population exposure is a weighted summary rather than an individual-level measure.
observations.subgroup: Citizens in democratic and autocratic regimes, political opposition, civil society, media, election institutions, and populations exposed to varying levels of rights and accountability.
observations.counterinterpretation: A global average or regime count can hide meaningful institutional variation, subnational resilience, protest capacity, and differences among electoral, liberal, and autocratic forms.

denominator.unit: countries in episodes of autocratization in 2025

autocratizers.unit: countries in autocratization episodes, nearly one quarter of the world's nations

population_in_autocratizing_countries.unit: percent of the world population, approximately 3.4 billion people, residing in autocratizing countries

episode_types.value: 24 stand-alone autocratization processes and 20 Bell-turns, where decline follows a recent period of democratization

regional_route.value: autocratization is not confined to one regime region; the report identifies effects in the European Union, the UK, and the USA as well as other world regions

observations.method: V-Dem Episodes of Regime Transformation methodology and regional analysis of autocratization episodes.
observations.uncertainty: An episode identifies a modeled pattern of regime transformation rather than a fixed endpoint or inevitable transition; timing and classification may change with later data revisions.
observations.subgroup: Citizens in autocratizing countries, opposition parties, civil society, journalists, courts, election officials, and international partners.
observations.counterinterpretation: Autocratization episodes can pause, reverse, or coexist with resilient institutions and civic mobilization; aggregate counts do not predict country-specific outcomes.

observations.period: 2025; expression, elections, media, and civil-society deterioration

expression_decline.unit: countries where freedom of expression is declining in 2025

election_quality_decline.unit: countries where quality of elections is deteriorating in 2025

media_censorship.unit: autocratizing countries, or 73%, using media censorship as a reported tactic

civil_society_repression.unit: autocratizing countries, or 68%, where repression of civil society has surged

institutional_route.value: backsliding is expressed through a connected control surface spanning information, electoral competition, media, and organized civic opposition

observations.method: V-Dem indicator-level trends and tactic analysis within autocratizing countries.
observations.uncertainty: Country counts do not measure severity, duration, or causal order; tactics can be coded differently across contexts and may be underreported where information is restricted.
observations.subgroup: Journalists, media organizations, opposition parties, civic groups, activists, voters, courts, and populations relying on independent information.
observations.counterinterpretation: Censorship or civic repression may coexist with alternative information channels and protest; declining indicators do not show whether domestic or international action will reverse the pattern.

observations.period: 2025; opposition suppression and Western democracy exposure

denominator.unit: V-Dem global and regional democracy assessment

torture_decline.unit: countries substantially degenerating in torture-related indicators in 2025

western_democracy_level.value: the level of democracy for the average citizen in Western Europe and North America is reported at its lowest level in over 50 years

usa_status.value: the report classifies the USA as losing its long-term status as a liberal democracy for the first time in over 50 years

opposition_route.value: suppression of opposition and civic freedoms can erode democratic quality even where elections and formal institutions remain in place

observations.method: V-Dem multidimensional indices and indicator-level assessment of liberal, electoral, expressive, and coercive dimensions of democracy.
observations.uncertainty: These are V-Dem's operationalizations and classifications, not a universal legal determination; country status and historical comparisons should be read with the report's coding and uncertainty framework.
observations.subgroup: Citizens in Western democracies, political opponents, journalists, civil society, minority groups, courts, and international democratic institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal electoral competition, courts, federalism, civil society, and public mobilization can provide countervailing resilience even during measured liberal-democratic decline.

related_sources.claim: V-Dem Dataset version 16 provides the underlying high-level indices, sub-indices, and indicators used by the report.
V-Dem's official release summarizes the 2026 report's global autocratization and Western-democracy findings.

boundary: This record adds V-Dem's global democracy measurement and regime-transformation signal on autocratization, expression, elections, media censorship, civil-society repression, torture, and Western-democracy decline. It is an index-based comparative assessment, not respondent-level data, an event-by-event incident census, a causal forecast, a legal judgment, or proof that every measured decline is irreversible.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official V-Dem Democracy Report 2026 PDF and release materials reviewed for global regime counts, population exposure, autocratization episodes, expression and election declines, censorship, civil-society repression, torture, and Western-democracy findings.
